title: Dragon Ball: Goku’s Story Across Four Series
summary: Explore four Dragon Ball titles and learn a simple way to compare them. Focus on Goku, the main journey, and each series’ place in the larger story.

What makes an adventure story exciting for you?

blocks.title: Part 1: Dragon Ball Begins
paragraphs: Akira Toriyama was a Japanese manga artist. He wrote and drew the Dragon Ball manga from 1984 to 1995. Manga means a Japanese comic, and it came before the anime.

The early story follows Goku as a boy. He lives far from towns until he meets Bulma. They look for seven magical Dragon Balls. Together, the balls can call a dragon that gives one wish. Goku also trains in martial arts with Master Roshi, makes friends, and enters fighting tournaments. The first Dragon Ball anime ran from 1986 to 1989 and showed this early story.

images.alt: A boy in a brown tunic, a girl with a ponytail holding a small silver gadget, and an old man with a straw hat gather around a glowing orange orb on a wooden courtyard table, with laundry, a bicycle, and a bag of more orbs nearby.

items.prompt: What are Goku and Bulma looking for?
items.answer: Goku and Bulma are looking for the seven Dragon Balls, which can call a dragon that gives one wish.

blocks.title: Part 2: Goku Grows Up in Dragon Ball Z
paragraphs: Dragon Ball Z continued the later part of the manga. The anime ran from 1989 to 1996. It began about five years after the first anime, so Goku was now a young adult and a father. His son was named Gohan.

An alien called Raditz told Goku that he was a Saiyan, a warrior from another planet. Goku then faced much stronger enemies, including the space tyrant Frieza and the magical being Majin Buu. The story became larger: Goku and his friends often fought to defend Earth. Gohan also trained and became stronger.

blocks.title: Check: Part 2: Goku Grows Up in Dragon Ball Z

items.prompt: What two important things do we learn about Goku in Z?
items.answer: We learn that Goku is a father and that he is a Saiyan from another planet.

blocks.title: Part 3: GT Takes a Separate Road
paragraphs: Dragon Ball GT was a Toei anime with 64 episodes. It ran from 1996 to 1997, after Z, but it was not based on Toriyama’s manga. Toriyama described it as a grand side story.

At the beginning, a wish changed adult Goku back into a child. He travelled through space with his granddaughter Pan and Trunks. They searched for the Black Star Dragon Balls because Earth would explode in one year if they failed. Later, Goku fought enemies such as Baby and the Shadow Dragons. GT was one possible continuation after Z, but it was separate from Super.

images.alt: A boy, a girl, and a teenage boy look out a round spaceship window at planets, with a pale orb marked by a black star sitting on a wooden desk beside a star chart.

blocks.title: Check: Part 3: GT Takes a Separate Road

items.prompt: Why do Goku, Pan, and Trunks search for the Black Star Dragon Balls?
items.answer: They search for them because Earth will explode in one year if they do not find them.

blocks.title: Part 4: Super Opens a Bigger Universe
paragraphs: Dragon Ball Super was another continuation after Z. Its anime ran from 2015 to 2018, and its story began after Majin Buu’s defeat, during the ten-year gap at the end of Z.

Super is part of the main line, meaning it is treated as the main continuation of the story. Goku met Beerus, a God of Destruction. He also learned that other universes existed. In the Tournament of Power, fighters from different universes competed against one another. Z often focused on protecting Earth, but Super made the setting much bigger by adding gods and many universes.

blocks.title: Check: Part 4: Super Opens a Bigger Universe

items.prompt: How did Super make Goku’s world bigger?
items.answer: Super added gods, other universes, and tournaments with fighters from those universes.

blocks.title: Part 5: How the Four Versions Differ
paragraphs: A simple comparison uses three ideas: starting point, big change, and result. Dragon Ball starts with Goku as a child, and his search for the seven balls begins his adventure. Z shows him as an adult and father, while battles for Earth become central.

GT changes Goku into a child again and sends him into space. It is a separate side continuation. Super continues the main line after Buu and introduces gods and other universes. Therefore, the order is not simply Dragon Ball, Z, GT, and then Super. Both GT and Super follow Z, but they take different story roads.

images.alt: A man and a boy stand at a sunlit study table covered with seven glowing orange star-orbs, a wooden staff, a folded martial-arts uniform, a small spaceship model, and a blue star map, with bookshelves and a bright window behind them.

blocks.title: Check: Part 5: How the Four Versions Differ

items.prompt: What is the most important difference between GT and Super?
items.answer: GT and Super are different continuations after Z: GT is a separate side story, while Super continues the main line.
